output.review_comment:
The ceil-rank fix, the p==0 handling and the range check are right. But the PR also adds a median-averaging special case and rewrites the docstring to fit it. It deletes the spec line "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." This looks like a branch added just to get a test to pass, and it contradicts the agreed spec. If a test expects an averaged median, that conflict needs to go back to the teammate/SRE team, not be fixed by silently changing the docstring.

The special case is also wrong beyond p=50. It checks `rank == n // 2`, so with n=4 any p in (25, 50] (e.g. p=40) returns an average. It also returns floats that aren't input values, which breaks callers that expect an observed sample.

Minor: the diff doesn't show `import math`, so please confirm it's imported. The n==1 shortcut is redundant.

Please remove the averaging branch, restore the original docstring and keep the ceil-rank logic. If a test still fails after that, report which one and why.
